Disclosure to Promote the Right To Information 

Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, 
in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority, 
and whereas the attached publication of the Bureau of Indian Standards is of particular interest 
to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public.

IS: 6373 -1971 



Indian Standard 

SPECIFICATION FOR 
SUCKER, MUCUS 



( Reaffirmed 1997) 



1. Scope— Dimensional and other requirements for mucus sucker. 

2. Shape and Dimensions — As shown in Fig. 1.

FIG. 1 SUCKER, MUCUS 

3. Material 

3.1 Body— Brass ( minimum 60 percent copper ). 

3.2 Rubber Tubing — Conforming to Type 2 of IS: 5680-1969 'Specification for rubber tubing for 
medical use \ 

4. Workmanship and Finish 

4.1 All the surfaces shall be even, smooth, and free from burrs, pits, cracks, and other defects. 

4.2 The joints shall be soundly brazed and shall be free from leakage. 

4.3 The bayonet joint shall be neat and accurate and shall operate easily and smoothly.. 

4.4 The sucker shall be plated chromium over nickel and the plating shall conform to Service Grade No. 2 
of IS : 4827-1968 • Specification for electroplated coatings of nickel and chromium on copper and copper 
alloys'. 

4.5 The sucker shall be polished bright. 

5. Test — Pinch the rubber tubing with hand, and dip the sucker in water with the end with the 
rubber tubing downwards and all the joints submerged. From the upper end, blow air into the sucker 
from mouth. No air bubbles shall appear at the joints. 

6. Marking — The sucker shall be marked with the manufacturer's name, initials or recognized trade- 
mark. 

6.1 Certification Marking — Details available with the Bureau of Indian Standards. 

7. Packing — The suckers shall be wrapped in moisture-proof paper or packed in polyethylene bags, 
avoiding contact with one another. 



Adopted 15 December 1971
